title: Relay record warehouse — canonical log over the network
description: Implements owner decisions D-CL35..D-CL45: relay seeding of sealed canonical segments as the point of record, inbound canonical P2P, signed sync plane, /ws/canonical mount (token then capability chain), dual-emit of every scene write, R-relay durability floor, SPEC-7 held state, per-verse warehouse settings, ts partial off the DB thread, local columnar BI, one relay per verse.

assumptions.A-1: D-CL20 scene writes (ImportGltf, DuplicateNode, RenameNode) stay Unsupported(DCl20), counted; reversal moderate
assumptions.A-2: warehouse_mode defaults off per verse; local dual-emit runs for every verse; reversal cheap
assumptions.A-3: R = ts_replication_factor regardless of ts_mode (mirror => 1); reversal cheap
assumptions.A-4: scene write = fe_runtime::scene_write::SCENE_WRITE_CENSUS (23 variants); governance writes not emitted; reversal moderate
assumptions.A-5: D-CL45 binds record (warehouse) relays only, not desktop relay mode; reversal moderate
assumptions.A-6: wrap delivery = recipient-sealed replicated rows (R2 precedent); reversal moderate
assumptions.A-7: capability issuance rooted in interim Manager authority; reversal high
assumptions.A-8: FE_MIGRATION_MODE=legacy_only kept as a local kill switch, not default; reversal cheap
assumptions.A-9: held carries no retry-after number; reversal cheap

partitions.note: Existing paths were checked with Glob/Grep at 92946362. Status 'future' marks files a slice creates. Gate slices (G1..G4) and integration slices (I1..I8) are serial; gates own only mod-declaration lines of their files, and integration owns behavior. A file appearing in a gate and a later integration slice is a serial hand-off, not a same-wave collision.
